A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PoseGAM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1's qualitative Appendix E to v2's Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-estimation results on five BOP datasets, architectural ablations in Tables 2–5, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds training-data ablations, computational-cost measurements, and evaluations after pose refinement in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Appendix E introduces an additional inference variant that applies the MegaPose refinement network to PoseGAM's coarse predictions. The core architecture, geometry processing, loss, and original inference procedure remain unchanged. Newly documented augmentations do not establish a change to the underlying training procedure.

E1.justification: Table 9 newly uses MegaPose 2M, containing ShapeNet and Google-Scanned-Objects assets, as an alternative training corpus and in combination with the authors' data. The five evaluation datasets and pose-estimation task remain unchanged; the four synthetic scenarios were already present in v1.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in Table 1 is unchanged. Table 10 adds comparisons with MegaPose-refined variants of MegaPose, GigaPose, FoundPose, and RayPose, extending the evaluated comparison pipelines without introducing a new named pose-estimation baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix E substantially extends evaluation with 10k-iteration training-data experiments measured by AR on an LM-O subset, shared MegaPose refinement across five benchmarks, and per-detection runtime and peak-memory measurements. These are additional protocols; the original experiments and their settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds direct validation of the dataset contribution: alternative versus combined training corpora and cumulative inclusion of centric, uncentric, variable-lighting, and appearance-edited data. This addresses a substantive question absent from v1's ablations, which examined architecture, view sampling, fine-tuning, and geometry injection.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new appendix tables continue the existing single-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their values. New results include LM-O subset AR of 28.5 with MegaPose 2M versus 34.3 with the authors' data, refined average AR of 56.5 for PoseGAM versus 56.2 for RayPose, and PoseGAM inference time of 0.67 seconds with 9.49 GB peak GPU memory. The refined scores are additional results under different conditions, not revisions to the original coarse scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and Equations 1–17 are retained, including the appendix derivation for rescaling normalized poses. No formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical definitions are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: direct multi-view pose estimation, geometry integration, and a synthetic dataset exceeding 190k objects. The claimed 5.1% average improvement and 17.6% TUD-L improvement are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly connects fewer reference views to low onboarding cost, acknowledges increased memory consumption, and interprets the dataset and refinement experiments. The existing explanations and limitations concerning deformation, transparency, and reflective objects remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly documents overlaying or underlaying other objects, JPEG compression, and Gaussian blur during augmentation. Tables 7–8 disclose comparator reference-view counts and 30M query images for the existing corpus. These are added disclosures; the original training budget, hardware, learning rates, and project link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix E newly positions the constructed dataset against MegaPose 2M in scale, object sources, and measured training utility. The related-work survey and cited research are otherwise retained; the altered Blender reference identifies the same software rather than a new work.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify the shared CAD-model and segmentation inputs, update cross-references and the appendix overview, and add acknowledgements. A quantitative Appendix E is inserted, with the existing qualitative section becoming Appendix F. The main narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Five new tables present computational costs, reference-view counts, dataset statistics, data ablations, and refined performance, substantially expanding the displayed evidence. Existing Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–5 are retained; Figure 7 moves from PDF page 16 to 17, and Table 1's caption gains an appendix pointer.

improvement.justification: v2 adds direct dataset validation absent from v1, tests performance after shared refinement, and exposes computational tradeoffs. The augmentation disclosures also improve reproducibility. These provide useful but bounded gains: dataset ablations cover a 10k-iteration LM-O subset, while uncertainty reporting and detailed timing and refinement settings remain unspecified.
